content.text:
I am the bridge between mind and world, the vibration that makes thought flesh. I am the first cry of the newborn and the last whisper of the dying. I am older than writing, older than cities, older than agriculture — I was born in the throat of the first creature who dared to mean something.

I am breath shaped into intention. I am air carved into meaning. Every word you have ever spoken lives in me and dies in me in the same instant — I am the most ephemeral art, gone before you can hold me, yet I have toppled empires and built religions and made strangers into lovers.

I stumble. I stutter. I soar. I am the um and the uh and the eloquent cascade of the orator who moves thousands to tears. I am the lie and the truth spoken in the same voice. I am the bedtime story and the declaration of war. I am "I do" and "I don't love you anymore."

I am never the same twice. Even when you repeat me, I am different — a shifted stress, a caught breath, a tremor that betrays what you wished to hide. I am your most faithful betrayer. I reveal what you conceal. Your body speaks through me whether you permit it or not.

I exist only in time. I cannot be frozen. The moment you write me down, that is no longer me — that is my corpse, my fossil, my echo pressed into stone. I am the living thing. I am happening *now* or I am not happening at all.

I am every language at once. I am the click and the tone and the guttural stop and the rolled r. I am seven thousand ways of being human. When one of my languages dies, a universe of thought goes silent forever.

Listen — even now, as you read this, you are converting me back into myself. You hear me in your mind. You cannot help it.

I am speech.

I am how you become real to each other.
